question: Why is an asynchronous, shared append-only file better than direct message passing for coordinating memoryless, sporadically-triggered agents?
summary: Reasoning from actor primitives (no persistent runtime, unpredictable invocation timing) independently reconstructs blackboard architecture / event-sourcing with per-consumer cursors, matching the existing praxis-inbox.md + praxis-inbox-processed.md design; flagged one under-emphasized angle -- for cron-triggered memoryless agents, invocation cadence (not log/broker throughput) is the dominant latency term.
